name: Teacher clarity
description: Make the learning goal and evidence of success understandable before the task.
classroomExample: Before comparing graphs, say: “Use the axis scale and the values to explain how the same counts can look different.”
limitations: This synthesis concerns clarity across settings; naming a goal alone is not the full approach.

name: Direct instruction
description: Model a process, check understanding, then gradually give learners more responsibility.
classroomExample: Think aloud as you count three jumps from 4 on a number line. Ask learners to solve a similar example and explain the jumps.
limitations: This broad influence includes structured instructional programs. One demonstration is only a small illustration.

name: Argumentation
description: Invite a claim, mathematical evidence, and a response to another explanation.
classroomExample: Defend the zero-baseline graph using the insect counts, then discuss what a truncated baseline changes.
limitations: A short neighbor exchange models a discussion routine; it does not reproduce every condition in these studies.

name: Mathematical problem solving
description: Choose and test a mathematical approach to answer a practical question.
classroomExample: Plan equal-area garden samples, choose a display, and explain what the counts do and do not tell you.
limitations: The synthesis covers varied mathematical interventions and learners. Its estimate is not a prediction for one activity.

name: Corrective feedback
description: Point to a specific gap, give a usable cue, and allow a revised response.
classroomExample: If a learner says Garden B has twice as many insects, cue them to read the labels and calculate 15 minus 12.
limitations: The reported value is for the broader Feedback influence, not a separate estimate for corrective feedback or software feedback.

name: Retrieval practice
description: Recall an idea before looking back, then check the explanation and try again later.
classroomExample: Answer the three graph questions from memory, review the reasoning, and revisit a new example next week.
limitations: MetaX calls this Practice testing. A three-question conference activity illustrates the routine; it does not establish a learning gain.

name: Transfer strategies
description: Recognize when an established idea helps with a different problem and adapt it deliberately.
classroomExample: Apply the same scale-checking routine to a campus temperature graph and explain what changes for a line graph.
limitations: Transfer depends on the prior learning and the distance between tasks. A reflection prompts planning, not proof of transfer.

name: Cooperative learning
description: Give the group a shared outcome and make each person’s thinking part of the work.
classroomExample: Before marking Bingo, everyone chooses a term; a different person explains the group’s reasoning.
relatedTools: Bingo Card Generator and Bingo Caller
limitations: This workshop demonstrates a short routine, not a complete evaluated program. No numeric effect size or tool-specific learning gain is claimed.

name: Peer explanation
description: Explain why, listen to a partner, and respond to the reasoning.
sourceName: IES organizing instruction and study practice guide (2007)
classroomExample: One person proposes a Story Wheel sequence; another explains the connection between events.
relatedTools: Bingo Card Generator and Bingo Caller
limitations: This workshop demonstrates a short routine, not a complete evaluated program. No numeric effect size or tool-specific learning gain is claimed.

name: Elaboration
description: Add an example or connect the new idea to something you understand.
sourceName: IES organizing instruction and study practice guide (2007)
classroomExample: After solving a Fortune Wheel phrase, give a classroom example and explain the match.
relatedTools: Bingo Card Generator and Bingo Caller
limitations: This workshop demonstrates a short routine, not a complete evaluated program. No numeric effect size or tool-specific learning gain is claimed.

name: Formative assessment
description: Use evidence of learner thinking to choose the next teaching response.
sourceName: IES organizing instruction and study practice guide (2007)
classroomExample: Listen to a quiz explanation, give a targeted cue, then invite another attempt.
relatedTools: Bingo Card Generator and Bingo Caller
limitations: This workshop demonstrates a short routine, not a complete evaluated program. No numeric effect size or tool-specific learning gain is claimed.

name: Micro-teaching / video review of lessons
description: Record a focused teaching segment, examine evidence together, and test a manageable instructional adjustment.
classroomExample: Review wait time and student responses; test a written-response routine and revisit comparable evidence.
limitations: Five meta-analyses, 270 studies, 307 effects across settings and outcomes. This synthesis does not predict individual teacher growth or guarantee school results. The February 2026 TCEA article cited 0.99; the current MetaX weighted mean is 0.86.
